__baseline_prompt__.text: An original scene presented as a school-life photograph: a student caught in an everyday moment at school. In the art classroom after lessons, an eighteen-year-old final-year student has interrupted tidying a drawing desk. The supplied reference guides her facial appearance and dark chin-length bob with airy parted fringe. She wears a soft gray school vest over a white shirt and navy trousers. Her individual presence comes through an absorbed, questioning expression, a small crease between her brows, and the warm natural light on her face. A large landscape drawing board stands upright on its bottom edge against the tabletop, held at its two side edges by her hands with her elbows comfortably bent. Its visible face carries a broad charcoal sketch of this classroom doorway, including its distinctive three-pane transom, with a dark human silhouette drawn in the center of the opening. The sketch fills the board and its simple shapes read at a glance. She has just turned this face toward the room; now her head and eyes turn toward the actual doorway at frame right. That open doorway has the same three-pane transom and is visibly empty. The drawn figure and the empty real opening form the unanswered question. Place the student and drawing on the left and the actual doorway beside her on the right side wall, close enough in depth that her questioning three-quarter face, both holding hands, the complete drawing, and the empty opening remain readable together. Rows of drawing desks and a green teaching board establish a working classroom. An eye-height medium-wide horizontal photograph places the viewer at the neighboring desk. Late afternoon window light grazes her face and the charcoal surface, while softer reflected light preserves the doorway detail. Natural skin texture, restrained color, and ordinary classroom wear give the moment the quiet credibility of a school drama still.
